methodological_limitations: Supervised ML algorithms assume observations are independently and identically distributed (i.i.d.).
Complex survey designs exhibit clustering (_PSU) and stratification (_STSTR), producing non-i.i.d. correlation structures.

Sample-weighted loss functions optimize for pseudo-population totals but standard errors from scikit-learn do not reflect design variance without Taylor series linearization or balanced repeated replication.
Individual user predictions in web deployment do not possess survey weights; inference estimates conditional probability P(Y=1 | X=x) for the specific patient profile.

Unweighted empirical metrics and weighted descriptive metrics must be reported separately; weighted metrics estimate population-level association, not guaranteed individual clinical diagnostic accuracy.
